traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Lindera benzoin (read 2026-10-18): "In the fall the leaves turn bright yellow". Colour ours.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Lindera benzoin (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): shrubs or small trees to 5 m; the lower bound is the model estimate's usual height (species-facts-2026-10-15).

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Lindera benzoin (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): drupe about 10 mm.

generator.params.note: Beaked hazelnut's values (a many-stemmed deciduous understory shrub), with a slightly smaller crown. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size.

allometry.note: 3 m at 15 years in the open, within FNA's 'to 5 m' and the model's usual 2-4 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FNA vol. 3: slender grey-brown stems; thin obovate leaves held level to ascending. The leaf card's petiole is 0.09 of its length, the flora's petiole against blade and petiole together.
